blocks.text: When chlorine gas is added to water it undergoes hydrolysis to a mixture of hydrochloric acid and chloric(I) acid: Cl2(g) + H2O(l) gives HCl(aq) + HClO(aq). Chloric(I) acid, HOCl, is a weak acid and partially dissociates in water to hydrogen ions and chlorate(I) ions, OCl-.

blocks.caption: Species formed on chlorination
rows: HClO in equilibrium with H+ + OCl-
weak acid, partial dissociation; the ratio depends on pH

blocks.prompt: What are the primary active species in the chlorination of water? Give the equations that show their production (Quick Check 13.6c).
blocks.explanation: HOCl and OCl-. Cl2 + H2O gives HCl + HOCl, and the weak acid then partly ionises, HOCl in equilibrium with H+ + OCl-. (The hydrolysis is itself a disproportionation of chlorine to -1 and +1.)

items: Cl2 + H2O gives HCl + HClO; HClO (weak acid) in equilibrium with H+ + OCl-: the two active species.
